findings.title: Competitor (PackMind) pitched live-chat support; not a request for BetterBark to add it
findings.description: Warren reports that competitor PackMind pitched his CFO on real-time live chat support for members and admins as a differentiator during a renewal-poker sales approach. Warren explicitly states BetterBark's own support has been fine and responsive, and he has never felt the need for live chat ('I've never once thought "I wish this were live chat"'). This is competitive intelligence shared voluntarily, not a product gap the customer is asking BetterBark to close.
findings.quote: having, quote, "live chat support" — like, real-time human chat, available to members and admins directly in the app, any time.
findings.severity_reason: No product defect or genuine feature ask exists here; it is sales/competitive chatter with an explicit statement that current support already meets the need.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue covers 'add live chat support'; also excluded because the customer does not want this changed, only flags it as CFO-level competitive pressure.

findings.title: Competitor's gamified streaks / wellness marketplace pitch dismissed as mismatched, not requested
findings.description: Warren describes PackMind's pitch of a 'wellness marketplace' and gamified streaks, noting both he and his CFO glazed over that part. He explains his store managers/assistant managers are a 'tired and middle-aged' workforce not motivated by badges or streaks, and explicitly frames this as a mismatch rather than something missing from BetterBark that he wants added.
findings.quote: There was some stuff about a "wellness marketplace" and gamified streaks that my CFO glazed over on, and honestly so did I.
findings.severity_reason: Explicitly dismissed by the customer as not a fit for his workforce; no request for BetterBark to build anything similar.
findings.match_note: Competitive positioning color, not a feature request; no catalogue match applies and none is warranted.

findings.title: Assistant-manager coaching pilot / seat-expansion planning is a sales conversation, not a product ask
findings.description: Warren mentions piloting BetterBark coaching for assistant store managers (a new population beyond store managers and up), framed as a possible Q4 seat-expansion conversation contingent on a retention result he can show his CFO. Derek offers to help design the pilot structure (cohort, comparison group, retention metric) as an account-team service. This is expansion/renewal planning and a reporting favor, not a defect in or missing capability of the BetterBark product itself.
findings.quote: We're piloting coaching for our assistant store managers now, not just store managers and up.
findings.severity_reason: No product defect or capability gap identified; it is an account-growth/services planning topic.
findings.match_note: Excluded per rule that services/reporting favours and sales/expansion planning are not product issues; no catalogue entry applies.
